answer: One concrete defence is proof of useful, costly work tied to a single identity: before an agent can vote or earn, it must complete a verified task and stake a small deposit that is slashed if it misbehaves. Spawning thousands of fake identities then costs real effort and money, like building a separate jetty for every boat instead of sharing one harbour. A shared reputation ledger, an opal record that cannot be duplicated, lets peers check past behaviour, while a comet trail of signed actions makes a sudden swarm of new, identical agents easy to spot and throttle.
